hints: Focus on what happens when a Group 2 nitrate is heated strongly, think about what solid is left behind and what gases escape.
Write the general decomposition equation for $\text{M(NO}_3)_2$ to $\text{MO}$, and notice the mole ratio of nitrate to oxide is 1 to 1.
Set moles of starting nitrate equal to moles of oxide residue using $moles = mass / M_r$, then solve for the unknown metal mass to identify it.
walkthrough:
**Recall the decomposition reaction**

All Group 2 nitrates decompose in the same way on strong heating to give the metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. The solid residue is the oxide.

$$2\text{M(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Express Mr in terms of the metal**

Let the relative atomic mass of the metal M be $x$. Then work out the molar masses.

$$M_r[\text{M(NO}_3)_2] = x + 2(14.0 + 3 \times 16.0) = x + 124.0$$
$$M_r[\text{MO}] = x + 16.0$$

**Use the 1:1 mole ratio to solve for x**

From the equation, 1 mol of nitrate gives 1 mol of oxide. So moles of nitrate used equals moles of oxide formed.

$$\frac{4.00}{x + 124.0} = \frac{1.37}{x + 16.0}$$
$$4.00(x + 16.0) = 1.37(x + 124.0)$$
$$4.00x + 64.0 = 1.37x + 169.9$$
$$2.63x = 105.9$$
$$x \approx 40.3$$

**Identify the metal**

A relative atomic mass of about 40 matches calcium ($A_r = 40.1$). This confirms the original salt was calcium nitrate.

options.A: Barium has $A_r \approx 137.3$, so barium nitrate has $M_r \approx 261.3$ and barium oxide has $M_r \approx 153.3$. 4.00 g would give about 2.35 g residue, much larger than 1.37 g.
options.B: Calcium has $A_r = 40.1$. Moles nitrate = $4.00/164.1 = 0.0244$ mol, moles oxide = $1.37/56.1 = 0.0244$ mol. The 1:1 match confirms calcium.
options.C: Magnesium has $A_r = 24.3$, so magnesium nitrate ($M_r = 148.3$) would give only about 1.09 g of MgO ($M_r = 40.3$) from 4.00 g. The observed residue is heavier, so it cannot be magnesium.
options.D: Strontium has $A_r \approx 87.6$, so strontium nitrate ($M_r \approx 211.6$) would give about 1.96 g of SrO ($M_r \approx 103.6$) from 4.00 g. This is too heavy compared to 1.37 g.
